findings.summary: Q1 (link syntax) and Q2 (tag representation) are marked as blocking and governance HITL policy requires interruption when blocking spec decisions are missing, but DEC7 explicitly chooses defaults to proceed without resolving them; this is a semantic mismatch about whether work can continue without stakeholder decisions.

evidence.note: Q1 is explicitly marked blocking
evidence.quote: true

evidence.note: Q2 is explicitly marked blocking
evidence.quote: true

evidence.note: HITL policy says to interrupt when Q1/Q2 not provided
evidence.quote: Blocking specification decisions are required (Q1 internal link syntax; Q2 tag representation) and are not provided.

evidence.note: DEC7 claims defaults/configurability avoid blocking
evidence.quote: Default to CommonMark with optional GFM extensions. Support both standard Markdown links and wiki-links ([[...]])

findings.summary: Lifecycle ordering implies the Search Index Plugin runs in the finalize hook after the Theme/Renderer has already rendered pages, yet rendered pages are expected to reference the generated search index assets; without a stated deterministic filename contract or a two-pass render, this is internally inconsistent.

evidence.note: Search index artifacts are written in finalize
evidence.quote: Hook: finalize(context) 7 search index artifacts written to output directory (optionally sharded).

evidence.note: Renderer runs in render hook (before finalize in the declared sequence)
evidence.quote: Hook: render(context) 7 HTML files and static theme assets written to output directory using context data.

evidence.note: Rendered pages must reference search index assets
evidence.quote: Rendered pages reference client-side JS bundle and search index assets via relative static paths.

evidence.note: Dataflow explicitly places rendering before search index generation
evidence.quote: Theme/Renderer Plugin renders ... 7 [render hook] 7 Search Index Plugin builds ... writes index artifacts

findings.summary: The static-site constraint/requirement states the site can be hosted/viewed without a server-side runtime, but multiple places rely on using a local static file server for verification/guidance; this creates ambiguity about whether file:// viewing is expected to work (especially for search index loading).

evidence.note: Constraint implies no required server-side runtime beyond the browser
evidence.quote: Output must be a static site ... with no required server-side runtime ... beyond what can run in the browser.

evidence.note: AT2 validation suggests using a local static file server
evidence.quote: attempt to open the site via a local static file server (or static hosting).

evidence.note: Risk register anticipates file:// restrictions impacting JS features like search
evidence.quote: Broken offline/local viewing when opened via file:// due to browser restrictions ... especially impacting search

findings.summary: Milestone M1 deliverable DL7 (minimal renderer stub) contradicts M1 exit criteria requiring faithful Markdown rendering (AT3 partial). A 'stub' cannot satisfy 'preserving formatting' verification.

evidence.note: M1 deliverable describes minimal stub
evidence.quote: Minimal Theme/Renderer Plugin stub that outputs one HTML page per note with basic formatting (no backlinks/tags/search yet).

evidence.note: M1 exit criterion requires faithful rendering
evidence.quote: Markdown Parser Plugin correctly parses representative Markdown files preserving formatting (AT3 partial).

findings.summary: DEC7 states tags support 'both YAML frontmatter and inline #tag syntax' but R18 (SHOULD) hedges this as 'option to configure which sources are used'. The decision appears more definitive than the requirement allows.

evidence.quote: Support tags from both YAML frontmatter and inline #tag syntax.

evidence.note: Requirement allows configuration of which sources
evidence.quote: SHOULD support extracting tags from both YAML frontmatter and inline #tag syntax, with an option to configure which sources are used

findings.summary: M2 exit criteria require '100% of expected backlinks appear' (AT9) but M2 deliverables do not include any test fixtures or definition of 'expected backlinks' for the test link graph referenced in AT9.
